en: These skills can be leveled up by playing the various courses at the batting center, and by progressing through Shinada's Side Story. View current skill levels by speaking to the clerk at the batting center.

As he progresses through the Side Story, Shinada will face old rivals as well as new challengers.
Facing them will also hone Shinada's batting skills.
Shinada-saaaan.
How's it going, man?
Yo.

How 'bout dropping by for some cleavage? For you, we'll keep
it cheap. The rest of these saps? Fuck 'em!
Thanks but no thanks. I'm screwed on time and there's work to be done.
Heh, bet you were just sleeping in. A man's gotta put in a proper day's work, ya know. Like yours truly.

Yeah, yeah. See you around. And tell that manager of yours
to ease up on the price gouging!
(What a day... I'm beat. Gonna go home and hit the sack.)
You cannot create Clear Data during a Premium Adventure.
Note that you cannot carry over data from a Premium Adventure game to start a New Game+.
(This is a booklet for 777 Town.)
Read the booklet?
(The booklet's titled 777 Town Walker. It says it has tips on playing pachinko and slots, and valuable information about 777 Town.)
(Here it talks about 777 Town. Apparently, it's an online pachinko hall that lets you play anywhere, anytime from your PC or cell phone.)
Hello. Welcome to Rose Hip.
Our establishment has an 8,400 yen minimum, along with a 3,150 yen cover charge. Requesting a specific hostess incurs another 3,150 yen fee.
Would you like to join us today?
I'll find you a hostess then. This way, sir.
You'd like to see Kaguya-san? This way, sir.
I see. We hope you'll come by again, sir.
I'm terribly sorry, sir, but Kaguya isn't here at the moment, I'm afraid.
Okay. I'll come back later.
We look forward to your next visit, sir.
(Damn. Don't have enough money.)
Actually...
Sorry. I'll hafta come back later.
(I'm gonna need at least 15,000 yen.)
Your check, sir.
You're coming up on your time limit, sir. Would you care for an extension?
Kaguya-chan's already agreed to go out with you, so shouldn't you be heading out about now?
No thanks. I gotta go.
Very well, then. Enjoy the rest of your stay.
You can't bail now, Saejima-san! You need to ask her out on an after hours date!
(Guess I gotta...)
Gimme an extension.
(Gah... Can't afford an extension.)
Nah, I'm goin'.
(Should I talk about somethin' else?)
(Maybe I oughta ask a question.)
(Maybe I oughta order somethin'.)
(Should I give her a present?)
(Should I ask her out on a date?)
(What should I talk about?)
(What should I ask about?)
(She already said yes. I don't needa push it.)
(She already turned me down once. I oughta back down for now and try some other time.)
Oh yeah! We are loaded today, buddy! Let us see your most popular girl!
That there was my fancy way of asking the club to bring us their girl, Kaguya-chan.
Saejima-san, if you make the girl do all the talking, she's going to think you're boring.
Sometimes you should be the one to bring up a topic to talk about. Or maybe you can try ordering something else.
Maybe start by asking her on a date!
Say what now? That's kind of a big thing to start with.
What are you talking about? No guts, no glory!
Ah, well. Guess I'll give it a shot.
Now be sure and try lots of different things!
You can't leave yet, man!
(Okay, how to start...)
Start by asking her on a date! I'm sure she'll go for it!
Where did you come from, Saejima-san?
Ah, what brings you to Tsukimino then? Work?
Yeah, but it wound up finishin' in less time than I thought.
Oh, so now you can relax and enjoy Tsukimino!
Wish it was that simple...
Nah, this ain't for work. I came here 'cause I wanted to.
Oh, well that's nice! I wish I could go and take a vacation on a whim like that.
It ain't exactly a vacation, either.
I went to Kamurocho for work before, you know.
Oh? For a hostess gig?
Yes. Just to make some money!
Impressive. Ya hopped on a plane to Kamurocho just to work in a cabaret club?
That's right. It was a lot busier than here, and the pay was better too.
Make a lotta money, did ya?
I did, but I spent it all.
How come?
I went shopping in Tokyo and hit up the clubs. Before I knew it, I spent all I earned.
So yer a big spender. Ain't nothin' wrong with that.
You think so? I feel like it would have been better if I'd been able to save at least some of that money.
No use cryin' over spilt milk. Think of it as a lesson learned.
But ya had fun, right? Then there ain't no problem.
You think so too, Saejima-san? To tell the truth, I don't actually regret it much at all!
Ya live by yer own rules, don't ya?
Tch, careless. How's that supposed to let ya make money? Maybe you should try goin' back.
Yeaaah, I can't really go. Now that I'm older, I'm kind of scared to cold-call clubs and go on interviews anymore.
Whaddya talkin' about? You're still young.
Not in this business! I'm practically an old maid!
Huh. That so?
Why'd ya come back? It must've been better than here.
I'd planned from the beginning to come back home after around three months.
That's not long. Where'd ya shack up?
Oh, I stayed at a friend's house. I knew someone who'd gone down to Tokyo for work, and she was kind enough to let me stay.
It's good to have friends.
What do you think about that kind of lifestyle?
Sounds fun. Livin' a life where ya get to move around from place to place might not be bad.
I think it would rather suit you, Saejima-san! You strike me as the sort who can make friends in new places pretty easily.
Yeah, that's true.
Not my style. Guys are better off settlin' down in a home. Somewhere permanent, reliable.
That's very prudent of you! You've got what they might call, real 20th century Showa values.
Weren't you born in the Showa era too...?
Wanna come to my place? There's plenty of work ya could do.
Oh? Do you run a cabaret club, Saejima-san?
Heh. It ain't anythin' like that.
Then no can do. I'm not exactly big on working, you know.
My job here is quite easy!
Should you be sayin' that to a customer?
You weren't born in Tokyo, were you, Saejima-san?
Nah, I'm from Kansai.
I knew it! You can tell if someone's from Kansai right away from the way they talk.
Hmph. How 'bout you?
I'm Hokkaido, born and raised.
So yer a country girl, huh?
Yep, that's me! Country through and through!
Where in Hokkaido?
Here in Sapporo.
Really? You don't got an accent though. Is that 'cause ya spent time in Tokyo?
No, I've just never had an accent, even when I was a child. People from Hokkaido don't have accents.
Huh. Now that ya mention it, no one I've met here's had one.
It's because we hear how they speak in Tokyo on TV. Maybe our grandparents might have accents, but our mothers and fathers certainly don't.
Bull crap. There's gotta be a hint of one at least.
Okay, maybe there are minor things someone from Tokyo might pick up on as an accent that I'm not even aware of. If there are, I'd be embarrassed!
Heh, yer safe for now.
That's good to know!
Hokkaido's a pretty big place. Maybe Sapporo's the exception.
Ya don't know yer own dialect, then?
It's not that I don't know it. Like people say "way" instead of "very." Not me, though.
I see. Maybe it's just a sign of the times.
Yeah. People from Aomori and other parts of Tohoku have a hella thick accent, though.
I'll bet. I can tell if someone's from Tohoku right away. Their accent's somethin' else.
But you have an accent yourself, Saejima-san. What's the big deal?
Kansai's different. We used to be the heart of Japan. That means that the Kansai dialect is true Japanese.
What!? What kind of logic is that?
Hella? What's that?
What? Do you not say "hella"?
Nah, dunno that one.
What!? You must! It's used all over the place!
Clearly not everywhere.
That's borin'. I came all the way to Hokkaido, and it's no different than drinkin' in Tokyo.
Well, Tsukimino is a pretty urban area.
Speaking of which, people from Kansai speak in Kansai dialect wherever they go, don't they?
Cause folks understand it. Ain't no need to do otherwise.
Oh, that's true. Since we hear it on TV a lot, most people do understand it. Enough that we can even imitate it.
You try imitatin' it.
What in the hey!?
Heh, ya've got the tone down.
How ya like me now?
Don't imitate people. Hearin' a fake Kansai accent pisses me off.
I guess you can tell off the bat, huh?
Yeah. I got a buddy who uses a half-assed Kansai accent, but it's so random that I've gotten used to it and don't get pissed no more.
It must really be something to make you give up, Saejima-san!
That a problem?
It's not that it's a problem, but I do wonder why.
In Kansai, even TV's in Kansai dialect. It's the norm for us. It's folks who speak in Tokyo accents that feel outta place in Kansai.
I guess Kansai really is a unique case.
Do you believe in ghosts or spirits, Saejima-san?
Yeah, I think they're real.
Y'know, I really can't handle stuff like that!
Heh, yer cute when ya get like that.
You kiddin' me? Of course they're not real.
But how can you know that for sure?
How? Well, have ya ever seen one?
Of course I haven't! The day I see something like that is the day I drop dead out of sheer fright!
Ya really don't gotta be so afraid.
I can see 'em, so I got no choice but to believe it. Hey! There's one behind ya right now!
Nooo, stop it! Please, I'd really rather you not tease me about this!
Hehe. What's got ya so scared?
I've just hated ghost stories ever since I was a kid. Anytime I'd hear one, I'd be so scared that I had to have the lights on the entire night.
Yesterday there happened to be a show about ghosts when I turned the TV on and so, thanks to that, I'm all sleep-deprived today.
Why are ya so scared?
A ghost I saw in a horror film as a child was terrifying. I think it wound up becoming some kind of childhood trauma.
Ha! A movie? Ya know it wasn't real, right? It was probably just some costume with a guy inside it.
It may have only been a movie, but wouldn't it be scary if it were real?
Probably. Like traditional Japanese ghosts don't have feet, right? I'd sure hate for one of those things to come after me in the night.
No, no, no, don't say that, please! You're going to make me imagine it!
Yer the one who brought this up, y'know.
There are no real ones. No sense in gettin' all spooked by 'em.
But Saejima-san, you were just saying that they DO exist!
Huh. Did I?
Yes! Please stop joking around about this! I'm really, really scared!
There are no real ones. I mean I've seen a kappa before, but that ain't the same thing.
A kappa!? Seriously? That's amaaazing! Where did you see it?
Ya can't handle ghosts, but kappa are okay? I don't get you.
Yer worryin' too much. Ain't nothin' gonna harm ya, so it ain't no big deal.
But it is! Sometimes I feel like there's someone in my room at night, or suddenly I'll feel a strange chill run down my spine!
You sure ya didn't just catch a cold?
I wish there were ghosts.
What!? Why would you say that?
If there were ghosts, it'd mean that we don't leave this world when we die, right? We'd get to stick around and enjoy it a bit more.
Ahaha! That's funny to imagine! I don't know what I'd do if you came back as a ghost, Saejima-san!
Heh, I'd be one vengeful spirit.
The other day, my friends from college called me up and we had our first LBBQ in a while.
Oh? Had some lamb barbecue, eh?
What's an LBBQ?
It's like barbecue, but with lamb. LBBQ!
We had a cookout with around twenty students and alumni. I haven't been back to my university after graduation, so it brought back memories!
Lamb barbecue's tasty! There's no point comin' to Tsukimino if ya don't eat some.
You really think so? A lot of people can't handle it, so I'm glad you like it, Saejima-san!
I don't eat it much. Lamb's not one of the meats I wanna have all the time.
Yeah, a lot of people can't seem to handle it. I hear the smell puts people off.
That's exactly it. I just can't stand the smell of it cookin'.
I should have figured. Why is that? It doesn't bother me at all.
Because yer a local. Ya get the chance to eat it while it's fresh.
When I was younger, I had some lamb in Tokyo that was way past bein' fresh. It stank so bad, I couldn't even eat it.
Really? It's a shame you came to dislike it without getting to know the true taste of it.
Well, I hear it's better these days. But I still can't shake that first time.
